micro_obligations.note: Normalize root parity by cube translation acting on all data. Since M is short its six holes split three even/three odd; covered target is a distinct odd vertex.
An adjacent pair among non-root holes can be added as a short matching edge, keeping u free and v covered; Z18 supplies the requested path for this four-hole supermatching.
The S9 cut has z in A and q in B while the three odd holes and v are all in A. Candidate y=w xor e_i is even and cannot equal q by preprocessing.

If u is in B, at most one of the three distinct candidates equals u; otherwise none are holes. A nonhole candidate is internally M_B-covered since its unique crossing neighbor is an original odd hole. Choose such a y, outside X_B and different from all original holes.
For u in B, A holes have even-minus-odd count -2. Equal internal parity coverage forces |X_A even|-|X_A odd|=2, so c is even >=2 and an even port a exists.
Y=(X_A minus a) plus w has even size c; D is a legal matching on uncovered vertices of M_A. Its union with M_A has exactly balanced four holes a,z,s,t.

K4 applies in dimension five with free even root a and odd target v. If v crosses, v belongs to Y since a is even, and D covers v. If v is internal, M_A covers v. No shortness/bipartiteness of D is assumed.

Removing matching D from an a-v Hamilton path cannot isolate any internal vertex; the only possibly isolated vertex is v when v belongs to X_A. Each deleted-D incidence supplies an exposed endpoint. Every port receives its distinct real crossing edge, including vh at isolated v, and w receives wy.

Appending fresh, pairwise distinct B endpoints to a path forest cannot create a cycle or connect distinct A components. Degrees leave v and X_B plus y as endpoints. Hence there is exactly one v-terminal path T_v and the other components compress to R on (X_B plus y) minus r.
3a r=y: R covers all X_B, disjoint from M_B. L_B has precisely two even holes u,q. N10 root u and covered target y satisfy y distinct from u and parity(y)=parity(q).
3a: expand R and append T_v at y. T_v interior lies in A, its only B vertex is y, so the result spans all vertices once and retains all original matching edges.
3b r in X_B: y is the sole overlap of M_B and R. k=M_B(y) is internally covered, while d=R(y) belongs to X_B minus r. Therefore k,d,y,u,q,r are distinct where required; kd is a legal replacement.
3b: removing yk and yd then adding kd leaves precisely holes u,q,r,y. The auxiliary ur joins two holes, leaving only same-even holes q,y.
3b: N14 with designated omitted hole y gives a 31-vertex B-y cycle containing ur and kd; ur and kd have disjoint endpoint sets. Deleting ur yields a u-r path retaining kd, regardless of parity(r).
3b: expand kd to k-y followed by the y-d transfer segment, restoring y once and its original edge ky. Expand other R edges, then append T_v at r; no artificial long edge remains.
For u in A, A has five original holes and B has only q, hence c is odd and >=1. D on X_A plus w has size (c+1)/2>=1, disjoint from u. M_A+D has exactly balanced holes u,z,s,t.

K4 applies with free even u and odd covered v, including when D covers v. Nonempty D belongs to the Hamilton u-v path, so deleting it separates u and v; only v can become isolated and real vh immediately attaches it to B.

After adding true crossing edges and wy, all B endpoints are distinct and fresh. The components remain a forest: one u-terminal component ending at r, one v-terminal component ending at s-prime, and compressed R on remaining endpoints. In particular r is distinct from s-prime.
4a y is one terminal B endpoint, other endpoint b belongs to X_B. R covers X_B minus b and is disjoint from M_B; L_B has exactly holes q,b.

4a: N10 with free root b, other hole q and target y applies since y is even like q and y differs from b. No assumption on parity(b) is needed. Orient its Hamilton b-y path to connect T_u and T_v, expanding R.
4b: y is covered by R, with d in X_B minus r,s-prime. Sole-overlap repair gives precisely holes q,y,r,s-prime; internal partner k is outside ports and all these holes.

4b: adding auxiliary r-s-prime leaves same-even holes q,y. N14 omitting y produces a cycle containing both auxiliary r-s-prime and replacement kd; deleting the former produces a spanning B-y r-s-prime path.

4b: expand kd and all remaining R edges, recovering y once. Attach the two terminal components at r,s-prime. Their interiors are disjoint and cover all A vertices together with R expansions, so the final result is a single Hamilton u-v path containing M.

For any coordinate separating distinct even holes z,q, the target half of M*=M-vh+hu has exactly one even hole and 1,2,3,or 4 odd holes. Values 1,2/3,4 invoke respectively S7,S4,S9. This does not require a further coordinate or geometric census.
A4 -> K4 -> S9 uses N10 and N14, while A4 -> S4,S7 are prior inputs. C6 combines these and Z18. Neither K4 nor N14 nor S9 uses C6, and G6 is unnecessary: no dependency cycle.

Only covered odd targets were used; the theorem remains conditional on A4 and named imported theorems. Six-hole free targets and larger hole counts are not consequences. The earlier twelve representatives remain the accurate exceptions to S4/S7 alone.
